subject: DataCove — deployment mode decision & network checklist
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Torres <alicia@datacove.com>, Mike Chen <mike.chen@datacove.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: DataCove — deployment mode decision & network checklist

Hi Alicia / Mike —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and the open network/ops questions we flagged so your team and our NetOps folks can line up next steps. High-level: DataCove indicated a strong preference for a Private VPC deployment due to compliance, but you wanted an apples-to-apples view of Dedicated capacity before finalizing. To make the Private VPC plan actionable we need to confirm the items below.

Open items (please mark answers inline or attach a diagram):
1) VPC topology: do you have a single management VPC or multiple application VPCs? Any overlapping CIDRs we should know about?
2) Connectivity preference: do you want AWS PrivateLink endpoints from Redwood, or VPC Peering/VPN? (PrivateLink is preferred for tenant isolation; peering may be acceptable if no CIDR overlap)
3) Egress requirements: will you require static egress IPs for outbound calls? We can provide a small pool (see attached checklist) but need to confirm NAT/egress owner.
4) Firewall/ports: confirm outbound ports to our endpoint (443) and any inbound ports for metrics/health endpoints.
5) TLS & auth: do you require mutual TLS or client certs? Any KMS/HSM constraints for key storage?
6) NetOps contact: please share the person(s) who manage VPC peering/privatelink and an available 45-min slot next week for a technical alignment call.

Attachments: redwood-privatelink-checklist.xlsx (stub) — quick list of the required CIDRs, port list, and sample CloudFormation snippets.

Proposed immediate next steps:
- Your NetOps shares diagram + CIDR ranges (if available) — Alicia
- Redwood NetOps (Ben, Priyom) reviews and identifies preferred connectivity (PrivateLink vs Peering) — Ben/Priyom
- Schedule technical alignment call (45 min) and capture RACI + tentative cutover window — all

If helpful, I can also run a short Dedicated vs Private VPC cost/latency comparison for your expected token throughput; we just need a rough QPS estimate.

Thanks — looking forward to the diagram and NetOps contact.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
T: +1 (415) 555-0192
Attachment: redwood-privatelink-checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Alicia Torres <alicia@datacove.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Mike Chen <mike.chen@datacove.com>
Cc: secops@datacove.com
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 19:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: DataCove — deployment mode decision & network checklist

Hi Tessa —

Thanks for the concise recap. Per your questions:

1) Topology: we run two primary VPCs — app-vpc (10.20.0.0/16) and mgmt-vpc (10.200.0.0/22). No other public overlapping ranges to our knowledge.
2) Connectivity: SecOps prefers PrivateLink where possible because of our strict ingress controls, but we may accept peering for internal non-prod. We attached our current network diagram.
3) Egress: We need Redwood to provide a small predictable egress IP set for allowlisting (outbound to third-party APIs). For inbound to Redwood endpoints we will allow connections from your PrivateLink endpoint.
4) Firewall: outbound to 443 only; health/metrics traffic must be over the PrivateLink connection and will hit our internal monitoring endpoint (we'll provide the endpoint host).
5) TLS: mutual TLS is required for data-plane connections; Control plane may use standard TLS. We use a customer KMS for key material and can negotiate HSM-backed keys if necessary.
6) NetOps contact: Mike Chen (mike.chen@datacove.com) and secops@datacove.com. Available slots next week: Tue 13th 10:30–11:15am PT or Wed 14th 1:00–1:45pm PT.

Attachments: datacove-net-diagram.pdf (network diagram stub)

We also answered the SOC2 question you asked on the call: we will provide the SOC2 cert during procurement.

Please confirm which slot works and if you need anything else beforehand.

Thanks,
Alicia
Director, Cloud Platform | DataCove
Attachment: datacove-net-diagram.pdf (PDF stub)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: DataCove — deployment mode decision & network checklist

Tessa / team — forwarding Alicia's answers. Quick tech notes before the NetOps call: 

- PrivateLink path: we will provision an NLB in our account per-region and present a PrivateLink endpoint service. That fits DataCove's mutual TLS requirement as long as the client cert handshake happens over the connection. We need to confirm whether DataCove will terminate TLS on their side for any callbacks.
- CIDR overlap: their ranges (10.20.0.0/16 and 10.200.0.0/22) look fine for peering, but prefer PrivateLink to avoid route table complexity.
- Egress IPs: we can offer a small CIDR of NAT egress addresses — typically we allocate a /28 per-tenant for non-shared egress; confirm this is acceptable for their allowlist. If they need truly static single IPs per logical application, we'll discuss NAT Gateway vs. proxy (there's an operational cost).
- Ports: 443 outbound; health pings over port 443 to the provided internal monitoring host. No extra ports expected.

Actionables for the call:
1) Ask DataCove if 10.20.0.0/16 is exclusive to them in their peering plans.
2) Confirm exact egress CIDR (we'll propose a /28) and whether they will allow that in their firewall.
3) Ask whether they require mutual TLS with client cert rotation cadence documented.

I attached Redwood's PrivateLink checklist (same as Tessa sent) for the NetOps folks. I'll prep a short RACI doc.

-ben
Ben Carter
Tech Lead, Infrastructure Integrations
Attachment: redwood-privatelink-checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Torres <alicia@datacove.com>, Mike Chen <mike.chen@datacove.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 10:42:00 -0700
Subject: RE: DataCove — deployment mode decision & network checklist

Hi Alicia / Mike —

Thanks for the diagram — very helpful. A few technical clarifications and our proposal ahead of the NetOps call: 

1) Recommended connectivity: PrivateLink in prod (isolated, fewer routing changes) + optional peering for non-prod.
2) Egress proposal: Redwood proposes allocating the following outbound NAT block for DataCove staging/prod: 18.200.34.240/28 (example from our egress pool). Please confirm that a /28 is acceptable for your allowlists; if you need smaller per-app IPs we can discuss a proxy layer but it adds cost and maintenance.
3) Ports/health: (a) 443 (TLS) from your VPC to our PrivateLink endpoint. (b) For metrics ingestion we will POST to your internal endpoint; provide hostnames and we'll validate DNS resolution over the endpoint during the call.
4) Mutual TLS: we support client certs. We'll exchange CA bundles in advance. Please confirm rotation cadence (30/60/90 days). For HSM/KMS integration we can use your KMS only for customer-managed keys on the control plane; data-plane encryption will be negotiated per SOW.

Prep items for the NetOps sync:
- Final CIDR confirmation (10.20.0.0/16 exclusivity)
- Approve egress /28 or request alternate approach
- Exchange CA bundle for mutual TLS test

Proposed meeting slot: Tue 13 Jun 2026 10:30–11:15 PT works for us. I'll send a calendar invite to lock it.

Cheers,
Priyom Das
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
